neighbours.label: A word inside a conventional name or epithet introduced by 'known as' or 'called' (the Elder, Corn Plant, Condolence Belts), vs the same subjects described without a naming phrase
fire: Pieter Bruegel, often called Pieter Bruegel the Younger, painted village scenes.
The rocky inlet is known to sailors as Dead Man's Cove because of the reefs.
This succulent is commonly known as Snake Plant in most garden centers.
The narrow lane behind the market was once called Tanners Alley by locals.
The bright comet of 1882, known as the Great September Comet, was seen by day.
The ridge is known locally as the Devil's Backbone for its jagged shape.
Their elite unit, called the Night Riders, carried out raids along the river.
In Spanish the hall is known as Sala de los Reyes because of its portraits.
quiet: Pieter Bruegel painted village scenes with many small figures.
The rocky inlet is dangerous for sailors because of the reefs.
This succulent is easy to grow in most garden centers.
The narrow lane behind the market was once full of tanneries.
The bright comet of 1882 was so brilliant it was seen by day.
The ridge is steep and jagged and hard to climb.
Their elite unit carried out raids along the river at night.
In the palace the hall is decorated with many royal portraits.

predictions: Words inside introduced names reach 0.35-1.3; plain descriptions stay under 0.06.
notes: Probe: Corn Plant 1.32, the Elder 0.80, Condolence Belts 0.68, Gate of Mercy 0.48, Battleship 0.34; same sentences without the naming phrase 0.02-0.05.
